previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, wheezing, and chest pain, consistent with an asthma exacerbation. She was initially somnolent, likely due to sedation from her chronic opioid medications, but remained alert with stable respiratory status. Her hypoxia improved with bronchodilators and steroids. Congestive heart failure was contributing, evidenced by elevated BNP and edema, and she responded to IV lasix. Due to concerns about incontinence, she declined higher oral diuretic doses. A urine culture grew E. coli, but as she was asymptomatic, antibiotics were not started, and follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider. Her warfarin dose was increased due to a subtherapeutic INR. She was discharged home on a prednisone taper, azithromycin, and adjusted medications, with instructions to monitor weight and adhere to fluid and medication regimens.

She was without leukocytosis, fever while admitted, and her 
abdominal exam as well as CT abdomen were without acute process. 
 Her anemia was mild and at her baseline.  She had one bowel

HCV viral load and CMV viral load were sent.

Stool studies were planned to be sent but the patient had no 
further bowel movements.  After much discussion with the 
patient, she decided she would prefer further work-up as an 
outpatient.  She was given information on follow-up as an 
outpatient and provided with sampling containers to provide 
stool samples to the microbiology department as an outpatient if

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
